title: the birth of the cousins
hook: the younger widow turns pale, the elder sends her maid in her place, and three very different brothers are born

segments.voice: Yesterday, Ambika shut her eyes, and Dhritarashtra was born blind. A widow too frightened to look.

Same palace, same sage, a different widow. Satyavati sends Vyasa to the younger princess, Ambalika. When she sees him, the blood leaves her face. She doesn't shut her eyes, as her sister did; her fear shows on her face instead. And the Kuru house is about to get three brothers: the blind one, the pale one, and one nobody planned for at all.
screen: `A DIFFERENT WIDOW.` → `SHE GOES PALE.` → `ONE NOBODY PLANNED FOR.`

segments.voice: Vyasa tells his mother: because she turned pale, the son will be pale, and that will be his name. Pandu, the pale one. He'll be a mighty prince, Vyasa says, and his own sons will be great. Two heirs now, one blind and one pale. Satyavati, still not at peace, asks for one more son from the elder widow. But Ambika can't face him again. She remembers his face and his smell, and does something no one expected: she dresses her maid in her own ornaments and sends her in her place. The maid isn't afraid. She rises when he enters, greets him with respect, and serves him. Vyasa is pleased. You are no longer a servant, he tells her, and your son will be virtuous and wise. He tells his mother everything, how the princess deceived him and how the maid honored him, and goes back to the forest. That son is Vidura. The text later says he is the god of dharma himself, born as a man because of a sage's curse; that's a story for another day. So here are the three brothers. One can't see. One is pale. And the son of a servant, born of a woman who simply showed respect, will grow up to be the palace's voice of wisdom, and, because of his mother's place, the one who can never be king. This is the generation before the cousins. Their sons will meet on the field.
screen: `PANDU, THE PALE ONE.` · `A MAID IN THE PRINCESS'S JEWELS.` · `SHE GREETS HIM WITH RESPECT.` · `VIDURA, THE WISE ONE.`

segments.voice: The maid met a strange, rough figure with respect, and it changed her life. Bring to mind someone who makes you uncomfortable, and without needing to like them, greet them inwardly as she did: you're welcome here. Notice what tightens, and what eases.
Pandu, the pale one, born because his mother's face went white with fear, now one of three brothers: the blind, the pale, and the wise.
Your line: she simply showed him respect. A servant's welcome gave the palace its wisest son. Day seven hundred twenty-three, done.

screen: `DAY 723 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: THE BIRTH OF THE COUSINS.`

howItsDone: Vidura's counsel to the king, the Vidura Niti in the Udyoga Parva, is read by some Hindus as a short guide to wise and honest living.

fork.setup: you're Ambika. Satyavati asks you to receive the frightening sage again. what do you do?
options: go again, eyes open this time.
send your maid, in your own jewels.
fork.reveal: she sends her maid, who greets Vyasa with respect, and Vidura is born.

original.note: Sanskrit Pandu: the pale one, the name Vyasa gives Ambalika's son because she turned pale.

trapdoor: what you thought: three princes born in a palace.
what it means: three sons shaped by fear, by pallor, and by a servant's respect.
what a scholar hears: the text later says Vidura is dharma itself, born as a man under a sage's curse.

chat.says: Who was Vidura's mother, and why did Vyasa bless her son?
options: A maid who met Vyasa with respect; he freed her and blessed her son.
Princess Ambika, who went to Vyasa a second time with open eyes.
A forest woman, who served Vyasa in his hermitage for many years.
chat.meaning: Ambika sent her maid in her place. The maid greeted Vyasa with respect, so he freed her from service and blessed her son, Vidura.

Vidura.meaning: the maid's son, wise in dharma, uncle to the cousins

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Ambalika and the birth of Pandu; the maid sent by Ambika and the birth of Vidura)
Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva (Vidura as Dharma, cursed by the sage Animandavya)

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli: Ambalika's pallor and Vyasa naming the son Pandu for it; Ambika's substitution of her maid adorned in her ornaments; the maid's respectful welcome; Vyasa freeing her from servitude and praising the coming son; Vyasa telling Satyavati of the deception.
Vyasa's blessing on the son is softened to 'virtuous and wise'; Ganguli's wording is stronger and was not used under the no-superlatives rule.
Vidura as an incarnation of Dharma under Animandavya's curse is only mentioned, not told.
The maid is described as a Sudra woman in the text; the script says 'servant' and 'mother's place'. A Keeper may wish to address caste more directly or not at all.
howItsDone names the Vidura Niti; confirm placement in the Udyoga Parva and phrasing.
